cards.explanation: The answer is themselves. God says, “Woe to the shepherds of Israel, who only feed themselves!” Then He asks, “Should not the shepherds feed their flock?” (Ezekiel 34:2) Feeding the flock is the whole job, friends, so a shepherd who only feeds himself is a one-man party with a LOT of guests missing.

The answer is True. God says, “You eat the fat, wear the wool, and butcher the fattened sheep…” That's eating, wearing and butchering, and the sheep get nothing out of any of it. The verse ends, “…but you do not feed the flock.”

The answer is sick. God says, “You have not strengthened the weak, healed the sick, bound up the injured, brought back the strays, or searched for the lost.” That's five jobs on the list, and none of them got done. I think this one hurts, friends, because these were the sheep who needed care the most.

The answer is with violence and cruelty. God says, “Instead, you have ruled them with violence and cruelty.” (Ezekiel 34:4) A shepherd is supposed to care for sheep, and this is the opposite. I think this one hurts to read, so let's take a breath together. The good news is that God doesn't leave it there.

The answer is that they become food for wild beasts. God says, “They were scattered for lack of a shepherd, and when they were scattered they became food for all the wild beasts.” (Ezekiel 34:5) A flock with no shepherd is in real trouble. That's a heavy picture, friends, and I think it shows why God cares so much.

The answer is False. God says the flock was scattered “…with no one to search for them or seek them out.” (Ezekiel 34:6) The sheep are on the mountains and the hills, and nobody goes after them. That's exactly why God steps in later.

The answer is that He will remove them from tending the flock. God says, “…I will demand from them My flock and remove them from tending the flock, so that they can no longer feed themselves.” They lose the job. A shepherd who only feeds himself doesn't get to keep the staff.

The answer is True. God says, “For I will deliver My flock from their mouths, and it will no longer be food for them.” He pulls the sheep out of the danger. The flock was being treated like a meal, friends, and God says that's over.

The answer is the LORD Himself! God says, “Behold, I Myself will search for My flock and seek them out.” The shepherds didn't search, so the LORD steps in and does it Himself. The search belongs to Him.

The answer is land. God says, “I will bring them out from the peoples, gather them from the countries, and bring them into their own land.” They get gathered from everywhere they were scattered. Then He brings them home.

The answer is False. God says, “I will seek the lost, bring back the strays, bind up the broken, and strengthen the weak; but the sleek and strong I will destroy.” His care goes to the ones the old shepherds ignored. That's what He means by shepherding “with justice.”

The answer is trample. God asks, “Is it not enough for you to feed on the good pasture? Must you also trample the rest of the pasture with your feet?” It's one thing to eat, friends. It's another to wreck what's left for everybody else.

The answer is horns. God says, “Since you shove with flank and shoulder, butting all the weak ones with your horns until you have scattered them abroad…” The weak ones are pushed right out. I think that's what makes God's coming judgment such good news for them.

The answer is False, and that's the good part. God says, “I will save My flock, and they will no longer be prey. I will judge between one sheep and another.” The flock that was hunted gets saved. And God takes care of the bullying sheep too.

The answer is My servant David. God says, “I will appoint over them one shepherd, My servant David, and he will feed them.” David was tending sheep when God sent for him (1 Samuel 16:11-13), and God had chosen him as king (1 Samuel 16:1). So a shepherd feeding the flock is a good name to hear, friends.

The answer is True. God says, “I will make with them a covenant of peace and rid the land of wild animals, so that they may dwell securely in the wilderness and sleep in the forest.” The wild beasts that once hunted the flock are gone. Then the sheep are safe, even in the wilderness.

The answer is blessing. God says, “I will send down showers in season…” and calls them showers of blessing. The rain comes right on time, and it brings good things. Fruit on the trees and produce from the land follow in the next verse, friends.

The answer is True. God says, “Then they will know that I am the LORD, when I have broken the bars of their yoke and delivered them from the hands that enslaved them.” He breaks the yoke Himself. And they come to know who He is.

The answer is that He is with them. God says, “Then they will know that I, the LORD their God, am with them, and that they, the house of Israel, are My people…” After all that scattering, the flock hears that God is with them. I think that's the line to hold onto, friends.

The answer is My people. God says, “You are My flock, the sheep of My pasture, My people, and I am your God…” He gives them a name and says whose they are. It's a warm way to close the chapter, friends.
